newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to raise flour, meat import duties - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia to raise flour, meat import duties - agency.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha said on Thursday Moscow would gradually raise import duties on flour and certain meats, but not on grain.
Zaveryukha, who is in charge of the harvest, was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying ministries were working on the matter, but he gave no specific rate increases or time frames.
"On grain imports, customs tariffs will not be adjusted, but on flour purchases, they definitely will be," he said.

The State Customs Committee, which is supposed to implement government decisions but has become more of a policy-making institution, said last month that it supported higher import tariffs on basic foodstuffs.
Zaverukhya is one of the main supporters of the ailing farm sector and is seeking ways to defend domestic producers.
Russian tariffs on flour imports are 10 percent. Tariffs on fowl, including frozen poultry, are 30 percent, according to the committee.

Russia is seeking to join the World Trade Organization but has upset Western food exporters periodically over the past 12 months by declaring its intent to introduce or actually levying duties on imported food.
Imports make up anywhere from one third to one half of domestic food supplies.
Flour imports, mostly from Kazakhstan and Ukraine, have soared in the past 12-18 months as Russia has gone through two poor harvests in a row.
